name: Conceptual Design & UX Principles
description: Translating behavioral goals and business context into a structured product concept. Covers Product Backlog management, User Story authoring, and the core UX design principles that govern behavioral product design: keeping interactions short and simple, making progress visible, ensuring success is prominent, and scaffolding user confidence incrementally.

subskills.name: Product Backlog Management
subskills.description: Structuring, prioritizing, and maintaining a product backlog derived from behavioral goals and user research insights. Covers backlog grooming, dependency mapping, MoSCoW prioritization, impact-effort matrices, and ensuring behavioral design requirements appear as explicit backlog items rather than being absorbed into engineering tickets.

subskills.name: User Stories & Acceptance Criteria
subskills.description: Writing behaviorally-grounded user stories in the format 'As a [actor], I want to [action], so that [outcome]'. Includes defining clear, testable acceptance criteria, writing Given/When/Then BDD scenarios, and ensuring stories capture the behavioral intent (not just feature functionality).

subskills.name: UX Principle — Keep It Short and Simple
subskills.description: Minimizing cognitive load and friction in interaction design. Applies Miller's Law (7±2 chunks), progressive disclosure, chunking complex tasks into steps, eliminating unnecessary form fields, and reducing decision fatigue. Measured by task completion rates and time-on-task.

subskills.name: UX Principle — Make Progress Visible
subskills.description: Designing feedback mechanisms that show users how far they have come and how far they have to go. Covers progress bars, step indicators, completion percentages, achievement unlocks, skill trees, and streaks. Grounded in Goal Gradient Effect (Kivetz et al.) — people accelerate effort as they approach a goal.

subskills.name: UX Principle — Make Success Prominent
subskills.description: Ensuring users feel the reward of task completion clearly. Includes celebration moments (confetti, animations, congratulations screens), success state design, positive reinforcement copy, and social sharing prompts at peak completion moments. Connects to Nir Eyal's 'reward of the self' and dopamine-driven engagement.

subskills.name: UX Principle — Scaffold User Confidence Incrementally
subskills.description: Introducing complexity gradually as users build competence and confidence. Applies Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development, scaffolded onboarding, beginner modes, contextual help that fades as expertise grows, and progressive feature revelation. Prevents overwhelm while growing user capability.

junior.description: Writes clear behaviorally-grounded user stories with acceptance criteria, applies KISS principle, and designs visible progress indicators.

mid.description: Manages prioritized backlogs with behavioral design items, designs compelling success states, and scaffolds onboarding flows for progressive competence.

senior.description: Establishes behavioral UX principles as design system standards; trains teams on Goal Gradient, scaffolding, and cognitive load theory; integrates principles into design review governance.
